compiled_state.description:
## Context / Problem

`sign_manifest` (src/rebar/llm/plan_review/generation.py) requires the tickets-tracker HEAD to be STABLE across a full `collect()` of the plan-review generation snapshot (before/after fence, MAX_GENERATION_ATTEMPTS = 3). On 2026-08-22, with peer agents draining enrich events at ~11 commits/minute (118 commits in 10 minutes observed on the tickets branch), `collect()` measured ~70 s per attempt — so the fence window (~70 s) always contained a peer commit and signing failed with 'plan review generation remained unstable after 3 attempts' on 19 consecutive `sign-review`/`review-plan` invocations spanning ~2 hours, for a review whose verdict was PASS and whose material never changed. The retry reasons alternated between before!=after HEAD movement and 'store-read-failure'. Consequence: the plan-review claim gate cannot be satisfied at exactly the times the store is busiest — multi-agent operation, the system's design center — and agents are pushed toward --force.

## Observed data

- sign-review wall time: 3m40s for 3 attempts (~70 s per collect()).
- Tracker churn: CLAIM_ENRICH/DONE_ENRICH/TICKET_DIGEST commits every 4-10 s from peer sessions.
- 797b-bbc4-01cf-42d5's attestation on the same day succeeded only on the 4th outer retry (~12 fence attempts).
- 5a30-d423-b1f5-4e33's attestation failed 19+ consecutive outer invocations (~57 fence attempts).

## Suggested directions (for whoever claims this)

The fence conflates 'the reviewed ticket's own material changed' (must re-review) with 'ANY commit landed anywhere in the store' (harmless for unrelated tickets). Scoping the stability check to the reviewed ticket's own material + related material fingerprints (already computed in PlanReviewGeneration) instead of the global HEAD would restore liveness without weakening the staleness guarantee; alternatively raise MAX_GENERATION_ATTEMPTS with backoff, or snapshot from a pinned commit rather than the moving HEAD.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] An attestation for a PASS verdict can be signed while unrelated tickets receive commits at >=10/minute; demonstrated by a test that commits unrelated events concurrently with sign_manifest and asserts success.
- [ ] A change to the reviewed ticket's own or related material between review and signing still refuses to sign (no weakening); existing behavior covered by a regression arm.
compiled_state.title: plan-review attestation signing has no liveness under sustained tracker churn
